articles.title: Rand Paul Formally Demands DOJ Probe Fauci for Perjury Over Gain-of-Function Testimony
articles.summary: Senator Rand Paul has submitted a formal request to the Department of Justice to investigate Anthony Fauci for alleged perjury during 2021 congressional testimony in which Fauci denied NIH funding of gain-of-function research — a claim contradicted by documented grant records. If the DOJ acts, it would mark the first criminal referral against the former NIAID director over COVID-19 origins. The implications stretch beyond Fauci: this is an indictment of the institutional cover-up that suppressed the lab-leak hypothesis for years.

articles.title: Doctors and Researchers Sound Alarm: Big Business Has Captured the Global Health System
articles.summary: Physicians and scientists — citing a landmark Indian Supreme Court ruling on predatory medicine pricing — are publicly naming what insiders have long known: the health system has been systematically colonized by profit-driven corporate interests at the expense of patient outcomes. The Supreme Court of India called out exorbitant drug markups as a structural injustice, not an anomaly. This is the pharma capture conversation that Western medical journals refuse to publish.

articles.title: Beta Bionics Allegedly Lied to Investors About iLet Device Safety — FDA Compliance Failures Exposed
articles.summary: Beta Bionics faces a securities fraud class action after its stock cratered over 37% when investors learned the company had allegedly misrepresented the safety, efficacy, and commercial viability of its iLet medical device to the FDA and the public. The lawsuit alleges executives knew about compliance failures and hid them — a pattern disturbingly familiar in medical device approvals. When the FDA's own oversight is compromised, patients and investors pay the price.

articles.title: Ensign Group Hid Patient Neglect, Falsified Staffing Data, and Ran Illegal Billing Schemes — Lawsuit
articles.summary: The Ensign Group, a major long-term care operator, is now facing securities fraud litigation after reports surfaced alleging the company concealed systematic patient neglect, manipulated quality and staffing metrics reported to regulators, and operated an unlicensed administrator scheme. The stock dropped 8% when the truth leaked — but patients in understaffed facilities paid a far steeper price. This is the institutionalized fraud that federal regulators were either unable or unwilling to catch.

articles.title: Pancreatic Cancer Cells Continuously Mutate to Evade Treatment — Half a Million Cells Analyzed
articles.summary: A sweeping analysis of nearly 500,000 individual tumor cells from dozens of pancreatic cancer patients reveals that cancer cells don't just resist treatment — they continuously reshape their genetic identity to stay ahead of it. This metabolic and genomic plasticity challenges the static tumor model that most oncology protocols are built on. The findings raise hard questions about why standard-of-care chemotherapy remains the dominant approach for a cancer with a five-year survival rate under 15%.

articles.title: IBD Patients on Immunosuppressants Got Live Vaccines by Accident — Zero Infections Followed. The Orthodoxy Has Some Explaining to Do.
articles.summary: In a study of 220 IBD patients on immune-modifying biologics who accidentally received live vaccines, not a single case of measles, mumps, or chickenpox resulted — directly challenging the blanket clinical prohibition on live vaccines for immunocompromised patients. This is precisely the kind of real-world safety data that should be driving guideline updates, yet the medical establishment continues operating on decades-old precautionary doctrine. Natural immune response, it turns out, may be more robust than the protocols assume.

articles.title: Hims & Hers Faces Fraud Lawsuit After FTC Complaint Exposes What Executives Allegedly Knew and Hid

The FTC's own action suggests Hims & Hers was operating in ways that regulators found deceptive — raising the question of how long the FDA and FTC watched before acting. When profit-driven telehealth platforms mislead patients and investors simultaneously, nobody wins except the executives.
